title: Tamsin and the Autopsy
premise: Insurance investigator Ines Thackeray receives a confession letter claiming the death of her estranged aunt Vivienne was murder — signed with Ines's own name, postmarked the day after the funeral. Returning to the family estate she fled fifteen years ago, Ines discovers the will names her sole heir, making her both suspect and beneficiary. Using her photographic memory to reconstruct the funeral week, she uncovers that Vivienne staged her own death to test which of her heirs would lie for love; the confession was dictated by Vivienne herself before dying of heart failure, a final lesson in loyalty versus truth. At the anniversary dinner, Ines closes the case by telling the family the whole truth — inheriting nothing but finally belonging.
about_author: O. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent a decade reading other people's grief in paperwork. They write mysteries about the lies families tell on official forms.

chapters.title: Postmark
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A confession letter arrives naming her as Vivienne's killer, postmarked after the funeral she didn't attend. Shaken by the impossible signature in her own handwriting, Ines travels to the Thackeray estate, where cold cousins greet her as stranger and heir alike. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve as she realizes only she can close this case.

chapters.title: The Sealed Room
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She examines the locked study where Vivienne died, her memory cataloguing inconsistencies: moved chair, missing medication, a second set of keys. Cousin Marcus warns her off; housekeeper Ruth slips her an old photograph of young Ines and Vivienne. Emotional beat: the investigator's thrill colliding with grief she never allowed herself.

chapters.title: What the Will Forgets
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Digging into the will's odd conditions, she finds letters proving Vivienne knew her heart was failing and orchestrated the scene deliberately, testing each relative's response. When Marcus confronts her with evidence framing Ines, she must choose: protect herself or expose the family's complicity. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into clarity at the cliff's edge.

chapters.title: Anniversary Glass
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the anniversary dinner, Ines lays out the truth — Vivienne's staged death, each relative's small lie, her own forged confession written under duress years ago and mailed by Ruth out of loyalty. The family fractures; the inheritance dissolves per Vivienne's final clause. Ines leaves with Ruth's friendship and her name cleared. Emotional beat: costly honesty becoming belonging.
